```{r} 
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dlookr)
library(reshape2)
library(ggstatsplot)
```


```{r}
gender_data_cgt <- read_excel("E:/Daten(x)/Daten(lw-r)/Abc/Doktorarbeit SJS/Analyse R-Statistics/controlgroup/Ergebnis Vergleich männl_weibl/gender_data_controlgroup.xlsx",
           sheet = 2, skip = 1)
```


```{r}
library(dplyr)
gender_data_cgt1 <- gender_data_cgt %>% 
  melt(cols = c("Male", "Female"),
       variable.name = "Gender") %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Treatment == "Leber_Para")


  
```

## patient data###
```{r}
patientidentifier_cgt <- read_excel("E:/Daten(x)/Daten(lw-r)/Abc/Doktorarbeit SJS/Analyse R-Statistics/controlgroup/Ergebnis Vergleich männl_weibl/gender_data_controlgroup.xlsx",
           sheet = 2, skip = 1 ) %>% 
  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Para") %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = 3:4,
               names_to = "gender",
               values_to = "numberofpatient") %>% 
  filter(numberofpatient== 1) 

## unknown gender dataframe
#test <- tibble(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`=c("9042861","9044899"),
#                     Treatment=c("Leber_Dic``lo","Leber_Diclo"),
#                     gender=c("Unknown","Unknown"),
#                     numberofpatient=c(1,1))

#patientidentifier_cgt <- rbind(patientidentifier_cgt,test)
  

```

```{r}

# gptaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# gptaltdata$`GPT Day11` <- as.numeric(gptaltdata$`GPT Day11`)

# gptaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
gptaltdata_long_cgt <- gpt_rawdata_cgt %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c("Edited_BfArM Nummer2", "Treatment"), 
               names_to = "Attribute", 
               values_to = "labreads")

# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data_cgt <- gptaltdata_long_cgt %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Para")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(Attribute, "DBSDay_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data_cgt <- filtered_data_cgt %>%
  group_by(Attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts back with the original data
gptaltdata_with_counts <- filtered_data_cgt %>%
  left_join(counts_data_cgt, by = "Attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_cgt_with_min_counts <- gptaltdata_with_counts %>%
  #filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_cgt_with_min_counts)

  
```

## alt data greater than 5 counts in all attribute###
```{r}
lparaalt_data_cgt <- left_join(patientidentifier_cgt,filtered_data_cgt_with_min_counts, by = ("Edited_BfArM Nummer2")) %>% 
  select(1,2,3,6,7,8) %>% drop_na(count)
```


```{r}
lparaalt_data_cgt %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% normality(labreads)
```


```{r}
dd <- lparaalt_data_cgt %>% 
  group_by(gender)
  
ggbetweenstats(
  data = dd,
  x = gender,
  y = labreads,
  title = "liver_para labvalues of ALT for male, female and unknown gender",  ###NEW###
  type = "np",
  ylab = "ALT U/L",
  ggtheme = theme_classic()
)

```


```{r}

  title = "liver_para labvalues of calcium for male, female and unknown gender",

)
```

```{r}

# gptaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# gptaltdata$`GPT Day11` <- as.numeric(gptaltdata$`GPT Day11`)

# gptaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier

  

# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data_cgt <- glucose_long_cgt %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Para")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "DBS|Day_Unknown"))  ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
glucounts_data_cgt <- filtered_data_cgt %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts back with the original data
gludata_with_counts <- filtered_data_cgt %>%
  left_join(glucounts_data_cgt, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 glufiltered_data_cgt_with_min_counts <- gludata_with_counts %>%
  #filter(count >= 3) %>% 
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(glufiltered_data_cgt_with_min_counts)

  
```

```{r}
  select(1,2,3,6,7,8) %>% drop_na(count)
```
